articles.title: Curious Katmai Cub Learns a Painful Lesson from a Porcupine
articles.summary: A young brown bear in Katmai National Park was caught on a livestream with a paw full of porcupine quills. The cub, 901jr, is the offspring of bear 901, a finalist in last year's Fat Bear Week. The quills should eventually work their way out, but the incident highlights the risks curious cubs face.

articles.title: Meet the Microbe That Hulks Out and Turns Cannibal
articles.summary: A single-celled protist named Euplotes gigatrox can transform into a supergiant that devours its own kind. Discovered in an aquarium filter in Curaçao, the microbe's transformation is triggered by abundant food. Researchers hope it offers clues to the evolution of complex life.

articles.title: Wool: The Surprising New Material for Bone Repair
articles.summary: Researchers at King's College London have transformed sheep's wool into a scaffold that helps regrow bone. In rat studies, the keratin-based material produced bone that was more organized and structurally sound than collagen, the current gold standard. Wool is also a sustainable, often wasted resource.
